title: Interior Painting in Micanopy, FL | Older Home Interiors
description: Interior painting in Micanopy, FL for older homes: crack and patch repair, wallpaper removal, tall ceilings, and enamel on original trim and doors.
heroIntro: Older interiors come with tall ceilings, deep trim, old wallpaper, and years of patching. We repair the surfaces first, then paint them with finishes that suit both the room and the house's age.

sections.h2: What we find inside Micanopy's older houses
body: Walk into a pre-war home in Micanopy and the walls tell a story. Hairline cracks fan out from door corners where the house has settled. Old patches show through under raking light from tall windows. Wallpaper may be hiding under one or two coats of paint. Trim and doors carry layer upon layer of enamel, sometimes with drips and runs from decades past, and the humidity that hangs around the oak canopy can leave bathrooms and closets prone to mildew.
Good interior painting in Micanopy, FL respects all of that. The goal is a clean, durable finish that still looks right in an older house.

We tape and mud settling cracks, fill dents and old anchor holes, and feather patches so they disappear under paint. Where wallpaper is coming loose or showing seams through paint, we remove it carefully rather than painting over it; our article on removing wallpaper without damaging walls explains how. Larger damage is handled through drywall repair and patching on the same estimate.

Brown rings left by a long-ago roof leak, or a haze of old smoke and cooking grease on a Micanopy ceiling, are sealed under a stain-blocking primer first, otherwise they ghost up through the fresh topcoat within weeks.

sections.h2: Finishes for old walls and original trim
bullets: Walls with character and imperfections: matte or eggshell, which hide flaws instead of highlighting them
Kitchens and steamy old bathrooms: satin or semi-gloss, so splashes bead off and a sponge takes care of the rest
Tall ceilings: flat, rolled evenly from proper staging
Original doors, casings, and baseboards: scuff-sanded and finished in waterborne urethane enamel
Stair railings and newel posts: the same hard enamel, since hands touch them daily
body: If a historic shade is already on the walls, bring us a scrap of trim, a paint chip, or a half-empty can from the shed and we will mix to it, checking full-size drawdowns against the old color. Low-VOC lines are on the table for bedrooms and nurseries too.

sections.h2: Keeping your Micanopy household running during the work
body: Nobody has to pack a bag. The crew shifts heavy pieces to the middle of each room, drapes them and the floors, and finishes one space before opening the next, so the kitchen and at least one bedroom stay in service. Expect about a day for a single room; a full interior falls somewhere from three days to two weeks, and old plaster with lots of crack work pushes toward the longer end. Because indoor work is not tied to weather, July and August are a fine time to book it while porch and siding jobs wait for the October-to-May window. Planning the outside as well? See exterior painting in Micanopy, or our main interior painting page.

faqs.q: Can you paint over wallpaper in my older Micanopy home?
faqs.a: We usually recommend removing it, since loose seams and edges show through paint and can lift later. If it is firmly bonded, the crew lead will explain both options.

faqs.q: Will paint hide the cracks in my plaster or drywall?
faqs.a: Paint alone will not. We tape, fill, and feather cracks first so the finish looks smooth, then use a flatter sheen on walls that still have some character.

faqs.q: Do you paint original wood trim and doors?
faqs.a: Yes, and we treat them carefully. Old casings and panel doors are degreased, scuffed, and spot-primed where bare wood or glossy oil shows, then coated in waterborne urethane enamel that dries hard enough to shrug off fingerprints and scuffs.

faqs.q: Do we have to move out while you paint the inside?
faqs.a: No. Rooms are tackled one after another with furniture and floors covered, so daily life in the rest of the house carries on around the crew.
